$comment: Claude Code hooks for the Gushwork design system. NOT the same thing as scripts/hooks/,
which holds this repo's git hooks — those guard pushing, these run on a teammate's machine.
check-update.sh exists because two documented gaps had no code behind them: autoUpdate is
per-machine and unsettable from repo settings, so it got skipped; and auto-update takes
effect only on the NEXT start, so the session that could warn you is the one that does not
know yet. See the header of scripts/check-update.sh.
check-approvals.sh is the last leg of REVIEW-LOOP.md — a ✅ reaction in Slack queues an
approval, and this is where it re-enters a session so the pass can be recorded. It is a
SEPARATE hook on purpose: one hook emits one JSON envelope, so two notices need two
scripts, and a broken approvals endpoint must not be able to silence the stale-version
warning, which matters more. It is inert without GUSHWORK_NOTICE_TOKEN, so it does nothing
for anyone who is not the reviewer.
startup|resume only. clear and compact re-fire inside a session someone is already working
in, and a second copy of the same notice reads as a bug. The script caches the network call
for 6h and stays silent when there is nothing to say, so a repeated start is cheap.
timeout 10: the default is 600s. This runs before anyone can type, on every session, on
someone else's machine. It must never be the reason a session feels slow.
brand-rule.sh is the floor under the skills. A skill loads only when the request matches its
description, and the five surface skills each name a specific deliverable, so a game, a poster
or a one-off that merely carries the Gushwork name loaded nothing and came back with the wrong
logo, font and blue (30 Sep 2026). This hands Claude the standing rule at the start of every
session, independent of the request, and points at the gushwork-brand skill for the detail. Its
matcher is wider than the other two on purpose: clear and compact DROP the session's context, so
a rule injected only at startup would be gone after the first compaction. The update notices stay
startup|resume because repeating them reads as a bug; repeating a rule does not.
SessionEnd runs log-activity.sh once more when a session closes, so a session that ends records its
final token totals. It does nothing unless a Gushwork skill ran in that session (the same gate as
every other row), and a closed laptop or a crash simply means the last skill, file or artifact row
carries the most recent figures instead.

welcome.sh (R48) greets by first name when a new session starts, so the person knows the skills are on. startup|clear only: resume and compact are mid-conversation, where a second hello reads as a bug. It is its own hook for the same reason check-approvals is: one hook, one JSON envelope, and a broken greeting must never silence the stale-version warning.
